Is Paige AI FDA approved for clinical diagnosis?
review.paige-ai.faq.1.answer.yes.paige.a: Yes, Paige AI received FDA approval in 2021 as the first AI-based pathology platform for cancer detection. It is cleared for use as an adjunct to pathologist review for identifying prostate cancer in digitized biopsy slides. The FDA clearance was based on extensive clinical validation showing over 99% sensitivity for cancer detection. Paige is also CE marked for use in Europe and continues to expand regulatory approvals for additional cancer types and applications.
review.paige-ai.faq.2.question.how.accur: How accurate is Paige AI in detecting cancer?
review.paige-ai.faq.2.answer.paige.ai.de: Paige AI demonstrates over 99% sensitivity in detecting prostate cancer, meaning it identifies malignant tissue in virtually all positive cases. In clinical validation studies, Paige reduced false negatives by approximately 70% compared to unassisted pathologist review. The platform was trained on millions of whole slide images from diverse patient populations, ensuring robust performance across different tissue types and patient demographics. Accuracy continues to improve through ongoing machine learning updates.
review.paige-ai.faq.3.question.what.equi: What equipment is needed to use Paige AI?
review.paige-ai.faq.3.answer.paige.ai.re: Paige AI requires digital pathology infrastructure including whole slide scanners to digitize glass slides and workstations for pathologist review. The Paige software integrates with major scanner vendors including Leica, Philips, and Hamamatsu. Cloud-based deployment requires internet connectivity for AI analysis, though on-premise options are available. Most academic medical centers and large diagnostic laboratories already have the necessary digital pathology infrastructure. Paige provides technical support for integration with existing systems.
review.paige-ai.faq.4.answer.no.paige.ai: No, Paige AI is designed to assist pathologists, not replace them. It functions as an AI-powered second opinion that highlights suspicious areas and provides diagnostic support. Final diagnosis remains the responsibility of board-certified pathologists who interpret AI findings in the context of patient history, clinical presentation, and other diagnostic information. Paige augments pathologist capabilities by reducing oversight errors, improving consistency, and enabling more efficient review of high-volume cases. The optimal outcome comes from combining AI precision with human expertise.
review.paige-ai.faq.5.question.what.type: What types of cancer can Paige detect?
Paige's FDA-approved algorithm currently focuses on prostate cancer detection in needle biopsy specimens. The company has algorithms in development and clinical validation for breast cancer, colorectal cancer, and other solid tumors. Paige's research pipeline includes extensions to immunohistochemistry analysis, biomarker quantification, and prognostic prediction across multiple cancer types. The platform is continuously expanding its capabilities through partnerships with leading cancer centers and ongoing clinical trials.
How much does Paige AI cost for a hospital?
review.paige-ai.faq.6.answer.paige.ai.pr: Paige AI pricing is customized based on institution size, case volume, deployment model, and specific features required. Typical enterprise implementations involve annual licensing fees plus per-case charges or unlimited usage tiers. Pricing generally starts in the hundreds of thousands per year for hospital pathology departments. The investment includes software licensing, integration support, pathologist training, and ongoing technical support.
